newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Miners drag Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Miners drag Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: SPI futures 2357 -18 US 30yr 6.60 +0.01
*Stocks close lower, Dow strength fails to overcome resource weakness, commodity prices. Volume 367.51 million shares, value A$1.11 bln, 1029 stocks traded, 319 steady, 331 up, 379 down.
Australian shares defied Wall Street's strength to close lower on Thursday with solid selling in the resource leaders ensuring the market lost ground.
At 4.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 13.9 points lower at 2,346.7.
The December share price index futures contract lost 18 points to 2,357 and was at a 10.3 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said the day's showing had been disappointing given a local interest rate cut on Wednesday and the strength of U.S. equity markets on Wednesday.
"I think that pretty much sums up the general feeling in the market," said director at Burrell and Co, Derek Bond.
Bond suggested the market may have been disappointed at the size of the interest rate cut, although he noted the size of the reduction had already been priced in.
"Perhaps the market was a bit disappointed at the size of the interest rate cut. Largely, it was already factored into current prices."
"There seemed to be quite a bit of weakness in a few of the resource stocks," Bond said, citing heavy turnover in mining leaders BHP, WMC and CRA.

"I think there is a little bit of uncertainty in the commodities market in general. Obviously, some of the supply and demand shocks we've seen, particularly the likes of the Sumitomo situation, have thrown a degree of uncertainty into the whole market."
Bond said the resource sector looked set to remain unpopular near term, while some mild profit-taking in the banks weighing on the industrials.
"The resource sector remains out of favour in the short term and in the industrials we saw a bit of profit-taking, particularly in the banking sector," he said.
Features included the turnover in the resource leaders. BHP topped turnover lists with several large lines going through the market.
Underlining resources weakness, the All Resources index lost 1.31 percent while the All Industrials lost just 0.29 percent.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about eight to seven, while about 31 percent of stock traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trading was active, while options trade remained only moderate.
Total options traded 36,672 (33,198)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 8,846 (7,085).
